bet.text: Keep it mechanically simple and let the programming do a lot of the work.

auto.text: A web app and a co-processor running ROS generate the points the robot has to reach and when to drop the intake and shoot.
A reply to the reveal praises a six-ball auto; another team's championship pit data lists five high shots.

cycle.text: Intake, over the bumper, straight into the feeder; wrong-color cargo can be rejected. A button quick-turns the robot toward the goal by odometry, vision lines up the swerve drive, and it shoots.
A team post says that in one Hopper qualification match it kept to the left lane, with 180 in the front court and 3538 in the right lane.

endgame.text: One arm pulls down on mid; the robot tilts by its center of gravity and the other, set at an angle, clips the high bar. The motion repeats for traversal.
A team post timed one match: into the hangar at 14, latched at 6.

changed.text: The first climber got hung up on a lot of things and needed much maintenance at one competition, so the team took it off and looked for the simplest method. The color sensor came after its first district event.
At the championship the climb did not latch onto traversal by itself until a fix in the fourth match.

outcome.text: 54-12-1 in official play; ranked 4 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 67.00, Hopper).

solves.text: Aim at the goal without a separate turret, even when the driver is facing away from it

facts.text: Turns the whole robot to the goal in place of a turret
A button, quick turn, aims it from odometry close enough for vision to take over
Another team's championship pit data lists 26 by 26 and weight 123 (units not given)

functions.name: Vector intake

solves.text: Bring the ball right into the throat of a compact robot

functions.type: over-the-bumper vector intake with mecanum wheels

facts.text: Gap, the diameter of a ball, about
Mecanum wheels
Chosen through testing and prototyping
The interviewer notes that it is not as wide as other teams' intakes

functions.name: Feeder

solves.text: Be quicker than the big hopper of its 2019 robot, without dead zones

functions.type: roller feeder right at the intake

facts.text: Two green rollers of about 2 inches grip the ball and guide it; they have their own motor, so they can help reject a ball without the whole path going backward
A bigger roller at the bottom removes a dead zone
Lexan on one side instead of rollers, which would need pulleys and gearing to turn the same way
Black rollers at the back put balls in the shooter

solves.text: Go anywhere for balls without worrying about having the other alliance's in the throat

facts.text: Added after the first district competition

functions.name: Shooter

solves.text: Shoot from almost anywhere without a turret

functions.type: fixed two-roller shooter with a two-position hood

facts.text: The hood alternates between two main positions
Speed changes between the two rollers let it shoot from almost anywhere on the field
Another team's championship pit data lists a fixed multi-flywheel shooter and five high shots in auto

solves.text: Line the robot up to the goal and keep odometry from drifting

facts.text: A second processor (captioned up board) runs vision and path planning, used instead of a Limelight
It finds the contours of the tape on the goal's rim and the angle from the camera to their middle
Bands of x and y values filter out ceiling reflections, an initial problem
Every shot updates the odometry from the camera, to work around drift

functions.name: Autonomous system
functions.type: web app and ROS path generation

facts.text: A co-processor running ROS generates path points and when to drop the intake and shoot
Data go to the roboRIO through NetworkTables, and the Java code works out the shot

solves.text: Replace a first climber that got hung up and needed maintenance each time

facts.text: Two arms; one is enough to hold the robot up and swinging
The second arm rises while the first pulls down on mid, hooks high, and the motion alternates to traversal
Both arms have double hooks; wire and elastic set their angles and keep them inside frame perimeter
A team post puts it among climbs of around 8 to 9 seconds from entering the hangar, with one match timed (enters at 14, latches at 6)

cost.text: Before the fix in its fourth championship match, latching onto the traversal rung needed manual work, and one attempt was missed

decisions.because: the drive does the turning, and after the pandemic season the team did not want super complex robots

decisions.choice: An intake opening of about 9 inches
decisions.because: it fits the ball, and compact worked very well for the robot

decisions.choice: A feeder right at the intake
decisions.because: the 2019 hopper had a couple of issues and was not as quick

decisions.choice: Lexan on one side of the feeder
decisions.because: rollers there would need a pulley and gearing system to turn the same way
the team can get away without buying a Limelight and it works perfectly fine

decisions.choice: Start the climber over with two simple arms
decisions.because: the first design got hung up and needed a lot of maintenance
the team found it vital to go anywhere without worrying about the other alliance's balls
